clue.text: Set fire to British vessel

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: An order to torch a British ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to something is to make it burn, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Wager European has no ill feeling for bugbear

parts.note: a wager is a bet
ire is anger, ill feeling

explanation.surface: A gambling European who bears no grudge, oddly offered as someone's pet hate.
explanation.walkthrough: BETE NOIRE is French for 'black beast', borrowed into English.
explanation.definitionFit: A bête noire is a person or thing one especially dislikes, which is exactly what a bugbear is.

clue.text: King George accepts that is revolutionary new rule

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the assembled letters are read backwards
accepts means the royal cipher takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as on British postboxes
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A king tolerating a radical new way of governing.
explanation.walkthrough: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher on British postboxes; 'revolutionary' turns GIER round to REIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a monarch's period of rule, and both words mean governing as sovereign.

clue.text: Rub out Republican source of inconvenience

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the three letters of the word rub are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to erase a Republican who has been a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rub out' looks like one verb meaning erase; 'out' is the anagram signal on RUB, giving BUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A burr is a prickly seed head that clings to clothing, so figuratively a persistent annoyance.

clue.text: Hear pin-up bust is lower

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hearing that a pin-up model's figure has dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' teases the pin-up's figure but is the anagram signal on HEAR PIN-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower in spirits means sadder or more miserable, so the comparative adjectives match.

clue.text: More than one spoke right before advance on day two

indicators.note: before places the abbreviation for right ahead of the rest

parts.note: A is taken as a short form of advance, as in the abbreviation adv. trimmed
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone on the right speaking up before a move on the second day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like the past of speak; it is a wheel's spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii are lines from a circle's centre to its rim, just as wheel spokes run from hub to rim; plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: That man notices leaders

parts.note: he is the pronoun for that man
ads, advertisements, are notices

explanation.surface: A man spotting who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notices' reads as a verb but is a plural noun, advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads are chiefs or people in charge, the same as leaders.

clue.text: Reduce support for dependent

parts.note: help is support
to less is an old verb meaning to make smaller, reduce

explanation.surface: A policy of cutting benefits for those who rely on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot cope alone is reliant on others, so dependent and unable to manage are near synonyms.

clue.text: Charlie leaves a group chat crudely making sign

indicators.note: crudely means roughly put together, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaves means goes away from, so the letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie quits a group chat after crude messages, making a gesture as he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes C out of A GROUP CHAT, and 'crudely' rearranges AGROUPHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To autograph something is to put one's signature on it, so to sign it.

clue.text: Rise up and start to speak skilfully

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: to do something well is to do it skilfully

explanation.surface: An exhortation to stand and begin speaking with skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or emotion that rises and grows is said to swell, as with a swelling sea.

clue.text: Disaster losing California in fellowship

indicators.note: losing means the state's abbreviation is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: a calamity is a disaster

explanation.surface: A catastrophe in California that ends with people pulling together.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations between people, the same companionship that fellowship describes.

clue.text: Resist losing first one

indicators.note: losing first means the opening letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: to face down is to resist, so face can mean resist

explanation.surface: Holding out against losing the very first match.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is the one in a pack of cards, so it stands for the number one.

clue.text: President embracing one he had succeeded

indicators.note: embracing means the president's name holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: Donald Trump was US president when this appeared
I is one in Roman numerals
he'd is the contraction of he had, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A president hugging someone who had made it.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph is to win or come out on top, so triumphed means succeeded.

clue.text: Turner departed clasping end of brush

indicators.note: clasping means the word for departed holds the letter inside it

parts.note: the late, as in the late king, means departed or dead

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: The painter Turner, dead, still holding his brush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' with brush suggests J.M.W. Turner the painter; here it is a machine that turns wood or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins a workpiece while it is shaped, so it is literally a turner.

clue.text: Number on street work unceasingly

parts.note: N is a standard abbreviation for number, as in algebra's n
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone at a house number on the street working without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something nonstop means doing it without pause, the same as unceasingly.

clue.text: Sick English prisoner: revolting criminal

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the word for prisoner is read backwards

parts.note: a lag, as in old lag, is a prisoner

explanation.surface: A sick English convict leading a riot, a criminal act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' reads as disgusting or rioting but turns LAG to GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal means against the law, which is what criminal means as an adjective.

clue.text: Religious leader is endlessly limp and lame

indicators.note: endlessly means each of the two words loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cleric described as weak and crippled.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque, so he is a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: A nation hosting former queen and empire builder

indicators.note: hosting means the word for nation has the word for former inside it

parts.note: a land is a nation
ex means former
ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A country playing host to an ex-queen and a conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great built a vast empire stretching from Greece to India.

clue.text: Settle back taking in the taxes

indicators.note: taking in means the reversed word encloses the word for the
back means the word for settle is read backwards

parts.note: to sit is to settle, as a bird settles on a branch

explanation.surface: Settling up backdated tax bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes TIS, which 'taking in' wraps around the clue's own word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithes were levies of a tenth of produce paid to the church, a form of taxes.

clue.text: Loudly urge second man to create storm

indicators.note: loudly means the words are said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: urge is hurry; the second man is Cain, Adam's son, so hurry Cain is spoken

explanation.surface: Shouting at a deputy to whip up a tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Adam is the first man and his son Cain the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical cyclone, an extreme kind of storm.

clue.text: Idiot lapses regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A fool who keeps making mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a donkey, and figuratively a foolish person or idiot.

clue.text: Aide's fist destroyed content

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: An assistant's fist smashed whatever was inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like a noun, what is contained; it is the adjective meaning pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: To be content is to be pleased and at ease, the same as being satisfied.

clue.text: Start to hand a poet a ten dollar bill

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: John Milton was the English poet of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: Handing a poet a ten-dollar note to get things going.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Hamilton's portrait is on the US ten dollar bill, so the note is called a Hamilton.

clue.text: Look both ways

definitions.note: to look at it, and the word is then checked from both directions

indicators.note: both ways means the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: to look at it, and the word is then checked from both directions

explanation.surface: Road-safety advice to check left and right before crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it, and the three letters read identically in either direction.

clue.text: Dawn is gold and yellow captured by artist

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: captured by means the artist abbreviation surrounds the heraldic colour

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Daybreak's golden and yellow light caught on a painter's canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora was the Roman goddess of the dawn, and the word means daybreak.

clue.text: First of sons he once treasured is killed

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A grieving parent's eldest, once cherished, has been slain.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shot dead is to be killed by gunfire, so shot stands for killed.

clue.text: Irritating, snide bastard ousted

indicators.note: ousted means thrown out, so the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: bitchy means spiteful or snide
b is a common abbreviation, as in b*****d, for bastard

explanation.surface: A spiteful, unpleasant person finally thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy skin is irritated or irritating, and the word extends to restless annoyance.

clue.text: Philosophy of returning praise is mocked at first

indicators.note: returning means the word for praise is read backwards

parts.note: to laud is to praise

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the previous word is used

explanation.surface: A school of thought whose praise is greeted with scorn at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Dualism is the philosophical view that mind and matter are two distinct realities.

clue.text: Had a chance to cover Russian retreat

indicators.note: to cover means the answer lies inside these words, covered by them

explanation.surface: An army's chance to protect a withdrawal of Russian troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' suggests a military withdrawal; here it is a country hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or villa, a holiday retreat.

clue.text: Minute spent in thought

parts.note: spent means used up

explanation.surface: A short time passed lost in contemplation.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder, so mused is a past-tense synonym of thought.

clue.text: Designs popular shelters

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
tents are shelters

explanation.surface: Plans for fashionable camping shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: Intents are purposes or aims, and designs can mean intentions, as in having designs on something.

clue.text: Crazy university times in New York

indicators.note: in means the letters are placed inside the abbreviation for New York

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them stand for times

explanation.surface: Wild college days spent in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is slang for mad or eccentric, the same as crazy.

clue.text: Trainee soldier acted strangely

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A young recruit behaving oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training to become an officer in the armed forces.

clue.text: Dish served by health farm one found outside unfinished slum

indicators.note: found outside places the numeral at the outer end, after the rest

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a ghetto is a run-down, crowded district, a slum
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Food served at a health farm, with someone discovered outside a half-built slum.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a pasta, and a plate of it is a common dish.

clue.text: Love from French poem

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
de is French for from

explanation.surface: A French love poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject, so it is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Roadside recovery runs about to find man

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is the UK's main roadside breakdown service
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
on can mean about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A breakdown service rushing around to locate someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the British motoring organisation that rescues broken-down cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron is a man's name, the biblical brother of Moses.

clue.text: Expected Liberal to fight

parts.note: due means expected, as in due to arrive

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician anticipated to come out fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people, and as a verb to duel is to fight.

clue.text: Central parts of abandoned shipyards needed to be coloured

indicators.note: central parts of means the middle letter or letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Derelict shipyards needing a fresh coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed means stained with colour, so it means coloured.
